draft_notes.explanation: Rejected draft blanket ban on covered shaved shapes. Enumerate visible-compatible rectangles, diagonals and monotone staircase masks; use endpoint visibility guaranteed by per-strip corner checks. Enumerate two-layer roles with same-layer pixel separation, exact occlusion consistency, partial overlap and colour visibility after reversal. Keep multiple explanations only when their completed outputs agree. No palette-order overwrite. Original fixture test2 has a diagonal and rectangle in the same layer whose bounding boxes overlap while their pixels remain separated. Use actual mask separation, not bounding-box separation, in program and sampling evidence; this includes native scenes and the supplied geometric mechanism.
draft_notes.limitations: Native shape grammar: rectangles, diagonals, or rows/columns shaved inward by0..1 cells per side at each step. Same-layer shapes separated by one cell; bounding boxes may overlap. Every colour partially occluded in one of the two layer orders and remains visible. Geometry extents inferred from native corner/strip endpoint constraints. Random labels accepted only when all valid visible parses agree; bounded100000scene attempts and200000search nodes. Explicit fixtures unchanged. Original simultaneous placement rarely packs3objects per layer and exhausted100000attempts. Random path now proposes each rectangle size1..16, enumerates legal non-overlapping positions, and samples one uniformly;12size retries per object before restarting scene. Counts remain independently1..3 per layer and all native size/position support remains possible. This changes the proposal distribution toward packable scenes, not the shape mechanism; explicit fixtures unchanged.
draft_notes.diagnosis:
The counterexample fails on demonstration pair 0 ([false, true, true, true]), not on the query. All five colours are listed below in visible palette-mapped colours, background 1:
- **Colour 4** (order 0) is a shaved rectangle: rows 0-6, cols 12-15, plus row 7, cols 13-15 only. It is partly covered by 6 (row 4) and by 2.
- **Its bounding box**, rows 0-7 × cols 12-15, contains no background. Cell (7,12) shows colour 2.
- **The bbox rule** therefore paints (7,12) with 4.
- **The generator's label** keeps 2 at (7,12), because the shaved 4 strip in row 7 started at col 13.
- **Other colours:** colour 9 is restored correctly; colours 2, 5 and 6 are unchanged.

Nothing in the visible input distinguishes "4 extends under the 2 at (7,12)" from "4's row-7 strip stops at col 13". The label depends on a hidden shave latent. This is genuine ambiguity, not a solver bug, so the repair rejects such scenes instead of special-casing them.

The query itself (diagonal 7 on top of the 2, 4 and 5 rectangles) is handled correctly by the bbox and diagonal rule.
draft_notes.constructor_issue: Hidden shaved geometry can be ambiguous, but not every covered staircase is ambiguous. Retain recoverable covered staircases through shape-and-layer inference, reject only distinct completed outputs or search failure.
